cards.text: It's the first day of the second month, in the second year since Israel came out of Egypt. The LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, in the Tent of Meeting. And friend, He's about to hand out the BIGGEST counting job I have ever heard of.

cards.question: The LORD speaks to Moses in the Tent of Meeting. Where is Israel camped right now?

cards.text: God tells Moses to take a census of the whole congregation of Israel, by their clans and families. And it is NOT a quick wave-your-hand-and-guess headcount.

cards.question: For this census, God wants every man listed by ___, one by one.
Not everybody in Israel makes this census list. Who does God want counted?

answers.text: Men twenty or older who can serve in the army
Men thirty or older who can serve at the tent
Every firstborn son from every single family

cards.question: True or false: God tells Moses to run this whole census by himself.

cards.text: Then God names the helpers, the leader of each tribe, from Elizur of Reuben all the way down to Ahira of Naphtali. Joseph, one of the sons of Jacob (Genesis 35:24), doesn't get one name on the list. He gets TWO: a leader for Ephraim and a leader for Manasseh, the sons of Joseph. And no, friend, there is no spelling quiz. I checked.
So Moses and Aaron, Moses' brother, take these leaders, the ones named by name, and get to work.

cards.question: True or false: Moses and Aaron gather the whole congregation on the first day of the second month, the same date the LORD gave the order.

cards.text: Then the counting starts, tribe by tribe, name by name, beginning with Reuben, the firstborn of Israel. Judah comes in biggest at 74,600, and Manasseh comes in smallest at 32,200. Friend, I once lost count of the chocolate chips in ONE batch. These men are counting a NATION.
Add it all up, and the total is 603,550 men, six hundred THOUSAND. But hold on, because one tribe isn't in that number at all.

cards.question: The tribe of ___ is not numbered along with the other Israelites.

cards.text: The LORD had already told Moses, "Do not number the tribe of Levi in the census with the other Israelites." Nobody forgot the Levites, though, since God has a different job lined up for them.

cards.question: Instead of counting the Levites, what does God appoint them over?

answers.text: The tabernacle and everything in it
The army and all its divisions
The census and all its records

cards.question: True or false: When the tabernacle moves, the Levites take it down, but the other tribes set it back up.

cards.text: This is the tabernacle of the Testimony, and God has a rule about any outsider who goes near it. Think Staff Only sign, but the sign was written by the LORD.

cards.question: What happens to an outsider who goes near the tabernacle?

answers.text: He must be put to death
He must wash and wait until evening
He must bring a lamb to the priest

cards.question: God gives the Israelites a plan for setting up camp. How is each man told to camp?

answers.text: By divisions under their own standards
All together in one single camp
Wherever each family chooses to settle

cards.question: The Levites camp around the tabernacle and watch over it, so that no ___ will fall on the congregation of Israel.
True or false: The Israelites do everything just as the LORD commanded Moses.

findings.problem: This story card has five sentences. Only the opening card may be longer than two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Aaron being Moses' brother is a Bible fact from outside Numbers 1, but no reference is supplied for it. Numbers 1:17 names Aaron without giving that relationship.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The card tells the total in verse 46 and the excluded tribe in verse 47, but it does not tell verse 44's twelve assisting leaders or verse 45's age, army and family qualifications. Its citation of Numbers 1:44-47 therefore starts wider than the content it uses.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The preceding card only teases that one tribe is missing. Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason that the blank is Levi rather than Dan or Asher, so this fill-in-the-blank depends on luck rather than an inference about meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This reproduces the wording of verse 53 and asks the baker to supply an unseen word. The earlier cards provide no sufficient basis for choosing wrath over famine or shame, making this a guess at the line's wording rather than a reasoned question about its meaning.
